newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto daughter firm to build $2.45 bln road link.
newsitem.headline: Suharto daughter firm to build $2.45 bln road link.

text.p: A conglomerate controlled by one of Indonesian president Suharto's daughters will start building a 5.82 trillion rupiah ($2.45 billion) road-rail link in Jakarta in April, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

It quoted Bambang Suroso, chief executive officer of PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, as saying on Sunday the flyover would consist of a 23.55-km toll road, a 21.25-km railway and a public road to link south Jakarta and downtown Kota.
A spokesman for the firm or affiliated companies was not immediately available for comment.
The firm is controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, 47, who is also involved in a long-running wrangle over Indonesia's Busang, one of the world's richest gold finds.
Soeroso said construction tasks such as soil surveys, drilling preparation, equipment mobilisation and personnel recruitment would start on April 21.
He said a joint venture agreement between Citra and two state-owned companies, railway operator Perumka and toll road firm Jasa Marga, would also be signed on that day.
Antara said Perumka will use the railway track to link 22 stations to a light-rail commuter service while Jasa Marga would operate the toll road.
Soeroso said 75 percent of the investment needed to construct the flyover would come from loans, 40 percent of which would come from abroad.
He said a syndication made up of some 61 banks which included foreign banks from Hong Kong, Canada and Singapore and 51 domestic banks would provide the loan.
Soeroso said the flyover would start operations in 2001 and the toll road was expected to accomodate more than 100,000 vehicles a day.
